result.title: Creative Priming: Decoupling Process from Product to Escape the Creative Paradox
result.summary: Many of the most consequential advances promised by AI, from curing diseases and inventing new technologies to formulating new scientific theories, are fundamentally creative acts. Yet creativity is uniquely difficult to learn because it faces a creative paradox: learning to repeat past examples of creative success makes those specific examples more likely to recur, inhibiting the very creativity desired. This work argues that creativity is better modeled as an explicit process rather than as a property of individual artifacts, and proposes to learn the underlying generative principles behind the creative process. In particular, to escape the paradox, we introduce creative priming (CP), wherein a trained priming model generates a prompt-specific primer that assists a response model in being creative, explicitly decoupling the creative process from response generation. The priming model learns through GRPO, rewarding primers that lead to responses that are novel, high-quality, and diverse, thereby reinforcing the process that yields creative responses without reinforcing any specific response.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张把创造力建模为显式的过程而非产物属性，提出 creative priming：训练一个 priming 模型为每个请求生成针对性 primer，辅助 response 模型作答，并用 GRPO 以新颖性、质量与多样性奖励 primer，从而强化产生创造性回答的过程而不强化任何具体回答。
AI.relevance_reason: 将「过程生成器」与「回答生成器」解耦、仅以最终产出质量奖励中间过程的做法，可能为 latent 推理状态的轨迹训练与贡献分配提供参照；但该工作为纯文本创造力任务，无视觉或多模态状态，其奖励设计能否用于 LVR 尚需核查。
